prompt: Give a short, rousing speech to annex the Wendy's parking lot on Route 9.
response:
My fellow citizens, look upon this sacred ground! For too long, we have gazed across the yellow line, treating this asphalt as a separate entity. We tell ourselves, "That is their Frosty machine, this is our pothole." But I ask you—when the bag rips and a loose nugget rolls under the fence, does it ask for a passport?

They call it a "parking lot." I call it a staging ground for greatness and spilled Sprite. We share the same air, thick with the ancient scent of sea salt and square burgers. We share the same seagulls, those winged liberators who respect no border and answer to no dumpster lid.

The time for half-measures is over. We will not be a people divided by a curb! We will extend the warm, greasy embrace of our jurisdiction to encompass every pothole, every faded white line, every mysterious sticky patch by the drive-thru speaker.

Onward, not to war, but to merger! Let the red wigs of the employees wave as one with our own! To the dumpster corral! To the menu board! To Route 9, now and forever, indivisible, with liberty and dipping sauces for all!
